definitions.explanation: To stand or arrange in a line.

examples.japanese: ここに{並|なら}んでください。
{人|ひと}がたくさん{並|なら}んでいます。
{本|ほん}が{棚|たな}に{並|なら}んでいます。
examples.english: Books are lined up on the shelf.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}の{前|まえ}に{長|なが}い{列|れつ}ができていて、みんな{並|なら}んで{待|ま}っていました。
examples.english: There was a long line in front of the shop, and everyone was waiting in line.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{先生|せんせい}の{言|い}うとおりに{二|ふた}つの{列|れつ}に{並|なら}んで、{静|しず}かに{歩|ある}き{始|はじ}めました。
examples.english: The children lined up in two rows as the teacher instructed, and quietly started walking.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pair: {並|なら}べる (transitive). Pattern: Xが{並|なら}ぶ (X lines up).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {並|なら}んでいる = 'is lined up' (in a line currently).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{列|れつ}に{並|なら}ぶ (stand in line)
・{人|ひと}が{並|なら}んでいる (people are lined up)
・{順番|じゅんばん}に{並|なら}ぶ (line up in order)
・{並|なら}んで{歩|ある}く (walk side by side)

PAIR: {並|なら}べる (transitive) - {本|ほん}を{並|なら}べた (lined up books). Queuing is culturally important in Japan.
